refugee_precision_finding.before_sentence: Section 11208(a)(1) would add fiscal year 2025 to the existing section 599D(b)(3) one-thousand allocation within the refugee admissions already allocated to the specified former-Soviet/Baltic national category described in (b)(2)(B).
refugee_precision_finding.corrected_sentence: Section 11208(a)(1) would add fiscal year 2025 to section 599D(b)(3). Within refugee admissions already allocated under section 207(a)(3) for nationals of the independent states of the former Soviet Union, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, the President must allocate one thousand admissions to the narrower section 599D(b)(2)(B) recipient category. That category consists of people who are or were nationals of those countries, are current members of the Ukrainian Catholic Church or Ukrainian Orthodox Church, and demonstrate public, active and continuous participation (or attempted participation) in the religious activities of that church. The larger nationality-based admissions allocation and this narrower religious recipient category are distinct.
refugee_precision_finding.before_limitation: The 599D one-thousand rule operates within the specified allocated refugee admissions and its defined (b)(2)(B) category; it does not add a universal or additional overall refugee quota.
refugee_precision_finding.corrected_limitation: The 599D(b)(3) one-thousand allocation is within the larger former-Soviet/Baltic-national refugee admissions allocation under 207(a)(3), for the narrower 599D(b)(2)(B) recipient category: are or were nationals of those countries, current Ukrainian Catholic or Ukrainian Orthodox Church members, with public, active and continuous participation (or attempted participation) in that church's religious activities. It is not an additional overall refugee quota or admission for every national or church member.
